md.overview.shop.back-office.payments.ch.name: Charge once
md.overview.shop.back-office.payments.ch.body: Checkout retries the same request. The order service treats a repeated checkout key as the order it already created, so a retry never charges twice.

yaml.overview.shop.back-office.orders.2.name: Runbook
yaml.overview.shop.back-office.orders.2.body:
# When orders stop flowing

Check the **relay** first. See the [outbox pattern](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html).

| signal | threshold | page |
|---|---|---|
| outbox rows | 10 000 | yes |
| relay lag | 60 s | no |

yaml.overview.shop.back-office.payments.name: Payments
yaml.overview.shop.back-office.payments.description: Takes money for an order, once, and says whether it was taken. Open it for how a charge is retried.

yaml.overview.shop.back-office.payments..name: A retried checkout repeats the same key, so a retry never charges twice.
Incident summary
yaml.overview.shop.back-office.payments..body: Checkout was slow for twenty minutes while the card processor timed out. The breaker opened, the fallback queued charges, and every queued charge was taken once the processor came back.

yaml.overview.shop.back-office.payments..name: Payment retry
yaml.overview.shop.back-office.payments..description: A flowchart, one of Payments' behaviours. It starts and ends at its marks; a decision's lines say where each answer goes.

yaml.overview.shop.customer-facing.store.description: An internal diagram: what the storefront is made of. Its pages meet through typed ports; its own ports sit on its walls.

yaml.overview.shop.data.1-model.description: The records as classes — fields, then behaviours — joined by the associations stored between them, each end saying how many and in what role. Order status is a type, so it draws no card of its own.
